procedure.step: The Ministry of Economy and Tourism registers the factory (outside a free zone, with MoIAT industrial licence and 40% domestic value added letter; about 3 working days).
procedure.authority: the Ministry of Economy and Tourism

procedure.step: The exporter logs into the ministry e-services portal, chooses the Certificate of Origin for India service, fills the application form, uploads required documents (proof of factory registration, commercial invoice, and for a trading exporter, the factory's purchase invoice), and submits the application.
The Ministry of Foreign Trade charges a certificate fee of AED 50 (band: invoice value up to AED 100000).
The competent authority issues the certificate before, at, or within 5 working days of export; it is valid for 12 months and covers one import.
The issuing authority requires the application to include HS code, description, quantity and value, with each item qualifying separately, and may request detailed cost sheets and a factory visit.

The exporter ensures direct consignment from the UAE to India (transit allowed under customs control with no operations other than unloading, reloading, storage) and indicates third-party invoicing if applicable.
The exporter keeps origin records, including cost breakdown, for at least 5 years from the end of the calendar year of issue.

The Indian importer claims the CEPA rate when filing the bill of entry, holds origin information under CAROTAR 2020, keeps supporting documents for at least 5 years, answers customs requests within 10 working days, and uploads the electronic certificate to e-Sanchit.

caveats.note: The '+' in the rule 'CTSH + VA 40%' is read as 'and' (both tests must pass); the agreement does not define '+', so this is Mansha's interpretation.
The duty estimate is on the shipment value given; India charges duty on the assessable (CIF) value at import, so actual amounts will differ.
CEPA rates reduce Basic Customs Duty (BCD) only; IGST, GST compensation cess, SWS and any anti-dumping or safeguard duty still apply.
The CEPA rate applies only if the product qualifies under the rules of origin and a valid certificate of origin is presented.

'Direct labour cost' and 'direct overhead cost' are not defined in the agreement; the agreement does not say whether the build-down and build-up methods use the same threshold apart from the 5-point Ex-Works adjustment.
A product that only undergoes minimal operations (listed in Art. 3.5) does not originate, even if it meets its product-specific rule.
Interpretation: de minimis helps only the tariff-shift part of a rule, not the VA percentage.
Cumulation is bilateral only; the last production process in the UAE must still go beyond minimal operations.
For retrospectively issued certificates, the agreement says box 8 for 'ISSUED RETROSPECTIVELY' but India's form says box 9; India's form governs entry into India.
UAE law sets a shorter 3-year minimum for record keeping; the CEPA's 5 years governs CEPA claims.

No official page read names the Ministry of Foreign Trade as the issuer of the India CEPA certificate specifically: its service page covers preferential certificates in general, and the India-specific page is still on moet.gov.ae.
A producer in a free zone is likely not eligible for Factory Registration; confirm with the Ministry of Economy and Tourism.
The Social Welfare Surcharge (SWS) is likely charged on the reduced BCD (no CEPA-specific text found); anti-dumping and safeguard duties likely still apply.
